newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian minister says cabinet did not discuss ERM.
newsitem.headline: Italian minister says cabinet did not discuss ERM.

text.p: The Italian cabinet did not discuss the question of the lira returning to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said.
"We didn't talk about it. We will talk about it at one of the next cabinets once the budget has been approved," Maccanico told reporters at the end of Saturday's meeting.
Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltorni confirmed that the issue was not discussed.

Education Minister Luigi Berlinguer said he expected a move on the lira re-entry soon. "A decision will be taken very shortly even if right now we haven't got a timetable," he told Reuters after the cabinet meeting.
Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco declined to be drawn on the matter. "These are the type of things you only talk about once it has been done," he told Reuters.
The 1997 budget is expected to be finally approved by the lower house of parliament later on Saturday. It will then pass to the upper house (Senate) for ratification.
Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi has said in the past that once the package had cleared the lower house Italy would seek to put the lira back in the ERM.

Some commentators have speculated that the government might even move this weekend. Most analysts expect the lira back in the currency grid in time for the European Union's Dublin summit on December 13-14.
The lira crashed out of the ERM in a 1992 currency crisis. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
